passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz.

passages.provision_quote: (2) procedure for each school to allow a: (A) parent or guardian of a student enrolled in the school; or (B) community member: (i) within the school district; or (ii) within the school district in which the charter school is located; to submit a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene (as described in IC 35-49-2-1) or harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); and (3) response and appeal procedure for each school to respond to a removal request submitted by a parent, guardian, or community member described in subdivision (2). (b) The response and appeal procedure established under subsection (a)(3) must require the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting.
passages.note: The enrolled text creates a removal-request and review process, so it leans toward restriction without matching any one rung's clauses.

Senate Yea on the conference committee report for a bill bundling Muncie school flexibility, third party vendor surveys, activism neutrality, school library removal procedures and criminal obscenity defenses; 10 of 49 voting Nay, so not near-unanimous.
passages.tally_quote: Yea 39 Education matters. Nay 10 Conference Committee Report #1 Excused 0 Not Voting 1

rows.reasoning: Donato sponsored HB 1447 (2023) and voted Yea on its conference committee report; the bill's new school library chapter lets a "parent or guardian" or "community member" submit "a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene" or "harmful to minors" and requires "the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting." That is review-gated removal, so it neither pulls a book on challenge nor removes on report, and the reviewer is the elected governing body rather than "a review committee of educators and parents". HB 1447 is also a multi-subject education bill and no statement of hers in the sources ties her vote to the library sections, so the act shows direction toward restriction without separating those rungs.
